key_insight: QPipe uses an LLM-driven multi-agent workflow to convert natural-language requirements into executable quantum applications for test optimization.
engineering_relevance: The approach lowers the expertise barrier for building quantum software by automating parsing, coding, review, execution, and verification steps.
method: Specialized agents handle requirement parsing, formulation, code generation, review, execution, and verification.
The system is evaluated on 20 real-world NL requirements tied to benchmark test-optimization problems.
Ablation studies test the role of code generation, task knowledge, review feedback, and multi-agent decomposition.
evidence_signal: Across 20 requirements, QPipe reports 100% average code compilation and 96.7% average execution/final-result combination, with generated solutions often outperforming an offline genetic algorithm.
watch_item: Performance depends on high LLM token cost and multi-agent coordination, so reliability and scalability may be sensitive to implementation details.
paper_title: Leveraging LLM-Based Agentic Systems to Generate Quantum Applications for Test Optimization
